subject: gr-qc
title_original: N-body next-to-leading order gravitational spin-orbit interaction via effective field theory
abstract: Using the post-Newtonian effective field theory (PN-EFT) formalism for spinning gravitating bodies, we derive the next-to-leading-order (NLO) spin-orbit potential and Hamiltonian for a system of N spinning bodies in general relativity. This extends the EFT treatment of the binary case to arbitrary N. We present two derivations: one in the generalized canonical gauge, and one based on the covariant spin supplementary condition (SSC), followed by a noncanonical transformation to canonical variables. In both approaches, the only new contributions beyond the binary case are three-body interaction diagrams. The canonical Hamiltonians obtained from the two EFT routes agree with the known ADM N-body Hamiltonian of Hartung and Steinhoff up to a canonical transformation.
title_relatable: Spin-orbit gravity equations extended from two bodies to N bodies
hook: A post-Newtonian calculation generalizes the spin-orbit interaction for binary systems to arbitrarily many spinning bodies, confirming agreement with an independent canonical framework.
summary: Gravitational wave models for compact-object mergers rely on post-Newtonian approximations that have mostly been worked out for two-body systems. Extending two independent effective-field-theory derivations to N spinning bodies, the authors find that all new physics beyond the binary case reduces to three-body interaction diagrams — no more complicated structures appear at next-to-leading order. Both routes yield Hamiltonians that match the established ADM result of Hartung and Steinhoff up to a canonical transformation, providing a consistency check across methods. The framework is relevant for modeling hierarchical triple systems and globular-cluster environments where multi-body spin effects may matter.
